distractors: Done without asking anybody first, though in full view of everyone it affects.
Done by hint rather than by statement, so that the other person has to work out for themselves what was actually meant.
Done informally rather than through the proper channel, in the open but without the paperwork the process would normally demand. The shortcut is procedural, and everybody can see it being taken.

Done in a rush, with the usual checks skipped to make a date somebody else set. The corners cut are visible at the time, and they turn up again months later in whoever inherits the job of putting them right.

Done reluctantly and only because you were told to, with the disagreement left obvious to everyone in the room. The manner carries the objection that the words themselves are not permitted to carry, and it is meant to be read that way by the person who gave the instruction.
